question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To look black
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. "To seem unfavourable".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"To look black"** means to appear ominous or unfavourable, as if something bad might happen. (अनुकूल न लगना)

 
 
• **Example:** The sky looks black; it seems like a storm is approaching.
 
 
 
• **"To seem unfavourable"** is the correct meaning of the idiom. It describes situations that appear to be adverse or problematic. (अप्रिय प्रतीत होना)
 
 
• **Example:** The future of the project looks black due to lack of funds.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom "To look black" aligns with the meaning "To seem unfavourable".

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: To roll on ice** (बर्फ पर लुढ़कना): This does not relate to the idiom "To look black". It refers to a physical action, not a figurative meaning.

 
 
• **Example:** The children love to roll on ice during winter holidays.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: To give an approving expression** (स्वीकृति व्यक्त करना): This option refers to showing approval or a positive expression, which is unrelated to the idiom's meaning.
 
 
• **Example:** He gave an approving expression when I presented my plan.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: To cry bitterly** (कड़वा रोना): This option refers to expressing sorrow through intense crying, which is not related to "To look black".
 
 
• **Example:** She cried bitterly after hearing the bad news.
